runtime_row.subject: Science
runtime_row.questionText:
Shown here is the extent to which two different animals can see in either direction without turning their heads. In animal 1, the eyes are placed towards the front of the head and in animal 2, the eyes are placed on either side of the head.

Since the placement of eyes in the two animals is different, their vision is also slightly different.

In the figures above, the grey part represents the parts that can be seen by both eyes at a time, whereas the white parts represent those parts that can be seen only by one eye at a time.

Animal 2 can see a broader area at any time compared to animal 1. Animal 1 can distinguish depths better compared to animal 2.

Observe the following food web. Classify the animals into two groups - one that would need to have vision as Animal 1 and another as Animal 2 in the diagram above.
runtime_row.answer: Animal 1: lion, jackal, kite, wild cat and owl. Animal 2: mouse, goat, rabbit.
solutionSteps: [1 mark] Animal 1: lion, jackal, kite, wild cat and owl. Animal 2: mouse, goat, rabbit.
runtime_row.finalAnswer: Predators (lion, jackal, kite, wild cat, owl) need Animal 1 vision; prey (mouse, goat, rabbit) need Animal 2 vision.

Animal 1 (left) has a narrow fan with a large shaded (grey) central region, showing a small total field but a wide binocular overlap. Animal 2 (right) has a much wider fan with only a narrow shaded wedge at the centre, showing a broad total field but little binocular overlap. Labelled 'Animal 1' and 'Animal 2' beneath. A second figure shows a food web drawn with pictures joined by arrows: a green plant (producer) at the left feeds a goat, a rabbit and a mouse; the goat and rabbit are eaten by a jackal and a wild cat; the mouse is eaten by an owl and a wild cat; the jackal and wild cat are eaten by a lion; and the mouse also leads to a kite. runtime_row.subject: Maths
runtime_row.questionText: An arch of a railway bridge, built on Chenab riverbed, is shown in the above diagram. It is a parabolic arch connecting two hills at P and Q. If the parabolic curve is represented by the polynomial p(x) = –0.0025x2 – 0.025x + 136. Observe the diagram and based on above information, answer the following questions : (i) Write the coordinates of point A. 1 (ii) Find the span of the arch. 1 (iii) (a) Write the zeroes of the polynomial using diagram and verify the relationship between sum of zeroes and polynomials. 2 OR (iii) (b) Find the values of p(x) at x = 100 and x = –100. Are they same ?
runtime_row.answer: (i) At x = 0, p(x) = 136 ∴Coordinates of point A = (0,136) (ii) Span of the arch = 238.5 + 228.5 = 467 units (iii) (a) Zeroes of the polynomial are 228.5 and −238.5 Sum of zeroes = −10 = −−0.025 −0.0025 = −coefficient of x coefficient of x OR (iii) (b) p(100) = 108.5 p(−100) = 113.5 ∴p(100) ≠p(−100)
solutionSteps: [1 mark] (i) Point A lies on the y-axis, so x = 0: p(0) = 136. Coordinates of A = (0, 136).
[1 mark] (ii) Span of the arch = distance between the two x-intercepts = 238.5 + 228.5 = 467 units.
[1 mark] (iii)(a) From the diagram, the zeroes of p(x) are 228.5 and −238.5; sum of zeroes = 228.5 + (−238.5) = −10.

[1 mark] Verification: −(coefficient of x)/(coefficient of x²) = −(−0.025)/(−0.0025) = −10 = sum of zeroes — relationship verified. [OR (iii)(b) p(100) = −0.0025(100)² − 0.025(100) + 136 = −25 − 2.5 + 136 = 108.5; p(−100) = −25 + 2.5 + 136 = 113.5. Since 108.5 ≠ 113.5, p(100) ≠ p(−100) — they are not the same.]
runtime_row.finalAnswer: (i) At x = 0, p(x) = 136 ∴Coordinates of point A = (0,136) (ii) Span of the arch = 238.5 + 228.5 = 467 units (iii) (a) Zeroes of the polynomial are 228.5 and −238.5 Sum of zeroes = −10 = −−0.025 −0.0025 = −coefficient of x coefficient of x OR (iii) (b) p(100) = 108.5 p(−100) = 113.5 ∴p(100) ≠p(−100)

runtime_row.subject: Maths
runtime_row.questionText:
Two representations of real numbers are shown below.

Which one is correct?
solutionSteps: [1 mark] Writes that Representation 1 is correct. In Representation 1 the rational numbers and the irrational numbers are two separate regions that together make up the real numbers, with the natural numbers inside the whole numbers inside the integers inside the rationals. Representation 2 is wrong because it nests the rational numbers inside the irrational numbers, and no rational number is irrational.

Representation 2 is a single rectangle holding five ellipses nested one inside the next, from the innermost outwards: 'Natural numbers', 'Whole numbers', 'Integers', 'Rational numbers', 'Irrational numbers'.

fields.questionText:
Two representations of the real number system are described below.

Representation 1: A rectangle headed 'Real numbers' is split into two adjoining regions. The left region is labelled 'Rational numbers' and holds three nested circles: 'Integers' containing 'Whole numbers' containing 'Natural numbers'. The right region is a separate compartment labelled 'Irrational numbers'.

Representation 2: A single rectangle headed 'Real numbers' holds five ellipses nested one inside the next, from the innermost outwards: 'Natural numbers', 'Whole numbers', 'Integers', 'Rational numbers', 'Irrational numbers'.

Which representation is correct?
solutionSteps: [1 mark] Representation 1 only is correct: rational and irrational numbers are two separate (disjoint) sets that together make up the real numbers, with natural ⊂ whole ⊂ integers ⊂ rationals. Representation 2 is wrong because it places the rational numbers inside the irrational numbers, but no rational number is irrational.

Based on the above given information, answer the following questions : (i) Find the volume of the cuboidal carton. 1 (ii) (a) Find the total surface area of a milk packet. 2 OR (b) How many milk packets can be filled in a carton ? 2 (iii) How much milk can the cup (as shown in the figure) hold ?

[1 mark] (ii)(a) Total surface area of a milk packet = 2(lb + bh + hl) = 2(15×8 + 8×5 + 5×15) = 2(120 + 40 + 75). [OR (ii)(b): Number of packets = volume of carton ÷ volume of one packet = (30×32×15)/(15×8×5).]
[1 mark] (ii)(a) = 2 × 235 = 470 cm². [OR (ii)(b): = 14400/600 = 24 milk packets.]
[1 mark] (iii) Capacity of the cylindrical cup = πr²h = (22/7) × 5 × 5 × 7 = 550 cm³ or 550 mL.
runtime_row.finalAnswer: (i) Volume of the carton = 30 × 32 × 15 = 14400 cm³ (ii) (a) Total surface area of a milk packet = 2(15×8 + 8×5 + 5×15) = 470 cm² OR (b) Number of packets = 14400/600 = 24 (iii) Capacity of the cup = (22/7) × 5 × 5 × 7 = 550 cm³ or 550 mL

runtime_row.subject: Maths
runtime_row.questionText: In the figure, ΔABC is a right-angled triangle, such that: AC = 25 cm, PT ∥ AB and SR ∥ BC. Find the area of ΔPQR.
solutionSteps: [1 mark] From the figure: RC = 50/5 = 10 cm and PC = 50/3 cm, so PR = PC − RC = 50/3 − 10 = 20/3 cm.
[1 mark] Since QR ∥ BC (as SR ∥ BC), ΔPQR ~ ΔPTC by the Basic Proportionality Theorem, giving PR/CR = PQ/QT.
[1 mark] In right ΔPQR, by Pythagoras QR² = PR² − PQ² = (20/3)² − (16/3)² = (400 − 256)/9 = 144/9 ⟹ QR = 4 cm.
[1 mark] Area of ΔPQR = ½ × QR × PQ = ½ × 4 × 16/3 = 32/3 cm².
